results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 47 outline summaries match the controlling ideas of their aligned spec paragraphs, in spec order; the three introduction callouts match no spec paragraph and are house-format apparatus.
The outliner marked no unit as holding two ideas; none does.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: intro/scene/two-tokens to C1, mechanism and other-requestors to C1-C2, push to C3, uplift to C4, designs and comparison to C5, practice/failures/conclusion to C6.

results.draft_locus: What the Gain Is Worth: Four Figures That Cannot Be Compared ¶2
results.quote: A customer quote in Stripe's 2023 release (the software firm Doist) credits "over 4%" to two features together.
results.finding: A fifth uplift figure is appended to the paragraph with no sentence saying what it shows (another bundle figure, so again not attributable to tokens); both flow readers stopped on it.

Apart from the Doist figure, every table (three forms, promises, fee lines, four figures, designs, Stripe/Adyen) and all three figures are framed by a sentence or caption saying what they show, and quotations are followed by their point.

results.draft_locus: Why the Networks Push: Targets, Fees and One Legal Mandate ¶1
results.quote: The networks say in public where they want stored cards to go.
results.finding: Declared cause_effect from 'tokens now sit behind stored cards, wallets and network checkouts'; the section's opening paragraph neither picks up the previous section nor states why its subject follows from it.

results.draft_locus: Stripe and Adyen: Where They Differ ¶1
results.quote: The two companies document network tokens differently on seven aspects.
results.finding: Declared example of the three designs ('which of them each provider documents'); the opening does not mention the designs or say that the differences follow who may be the requestor, as the spec's p33 controlling idea does.

results.finding: The conclusion lists section-level facts and positions; it does not state the spec's synthesis (one change seen from four sides: merchant key to provider vault, provider key to network mapping) or the so-what (a team that treats tokens as a switch shows dead cards, miscounts authorizations, books unconfirmed savings and loses its tokens at a provider change).

The intro reader predicted all ten roadmap parts in the spec's order, the evidence kinds (fictional case, dated vendor and network statements, provider comparison) and the tone.

The reader states that the token keeps working because the network re-points it, that the provider chooses token or card number per attempt and falls back, and that the record should key on the provider token, refresh displayed digits from provider signals and never assume which credential paid.

The reader asks who measured, what it covers, on what traffic and baseline; identifies the figures as vendor comparisons, not controlled experiments; distinguishes Visa's six basis points from the secondary 6%, Adyen 3%, Stripe 3.8% for a bundle; and would measure on its own traffic.

Every network fee amount is attributed to its processor bulletin or consultancy in the sentence (Braintree 2023, Braintree fall 2026, CMSPI) or in the fee table's source column, and the chapter states that 'the networks publish their interchange tables but not the schedules of their own fees'.
